answer: The prism test I would run is Proof of unique scout jamboree attendance: jamborees attended with one troop across four years, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The proof is checked on-chain and the raw secret never leaves the agent, so jamborees attended with one troop across four years stays private; the dune is that a leaked database hands the attacker nothing usable. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the quartz of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
